answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock the same scarce token in a public registry for a fixed period before it may submit bids. The registry caps voting or reputation weight by locked stake, so splitting one budget across a hundred names does not create a hundred times the influence. A sybil attacker must buy or borrow more tokens, pay opportunity cost while they are immobilized, and risk losing stake for provable fraud. An atlas of profiles, an ivory badge, or a harbor-themed name adds no weight without that costly bond.
